predecessors.name: Mataram Sultanate
predecessors.text: 'the eastern half of the Sultanate of Mataram in central Java was given to Pakubuwono III with Surakarta as its capital' (Treaty of Giyanti, 13 February 1755)

successors.name: Dutch East Indies
successors.text: the Sunanate's lands after 'the territory of Surakarta Sunanate were reduced much further after the Java War'

ledger.x: 13 February 1755: the Treaty of Giyanti makes Surakarta a state under Pakubuwono III.
1755: the Sunanate is born a protectorate of the Dutch East India Company.
17 March 1757: the Treaty of Salatiga cuts the Mangkunegaran princedom out of Surakarta.
1799: the Company protectorate ends; the Batavian Republic follows.
1806: protectorate of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
1811: the Dutch protectorate lapses when Britain takes Java.
1811: protectorate of the British East India Company.
1816: the British protectorate ends; Java returns to the Dutch.
1830: this dossier ends with the Dutch cut of the mancanagara and the deposition of Pakubuwono VI; the infobox protectorate runs on to 1942 for the rump Sunanate, which is not drawn here.
1830: Pakubuwono VI is deposed and exiled to Ambon, 'the Dutch suspected him of working with Diponegoro'; the rump princely states 'no longer posed a threat to the Dutch'.

wars.name: Java War
wars.outcome: Pakubuwono VI, suspected of working with Diponegoro, was deposed and exiled to Ambon in 1830; the Sunanate lost most of its remaining outlying territory to the Dutch.

certainty.note: No boundary lines are named on the pages opened: the Giyanti halves, the Mangkunegaran cut and the mancanagara are all approximate.
